extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. MMMU includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: Benchmark collection takes three stages. Firstly, the authors went through common university majors to decide what subjects should be included based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted. They selected 30 subjects from six different disciplines. In the second stage, they recruited over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions collected from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials across 30 subjects in six disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two steps of data cleaning were performed. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by the authors to eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format. In the third and final stage, authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. Annotators followed a detailed protocol including guidelines on data format (JSON), naming conventions, quality control, handling ambiguities, and ethical considerations including copyright compliance. Annotations include question text, answer options (for multiple-choice), correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A secondary review team rigorously vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits of random samples from the dataset were conducted to ensure sustained quality and consistency. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process and collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students (including co-authors) specializing in the 30 selected subjects/majors. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students (3 student experts per subject) represented a wide range of experts in the corresponding 30 subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is hosted at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/ with a live-updating leaderboard. Multiple versions have been released with a detailed version change log documenting updates from v1 (Nov.27, 2023) to v4 (June.13, 2024), including additions of new model results and corrections to errors.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotators were instructed to avoid collecting questions that contain any private information, in compliance with privacy laws and ethical standards in data handling.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note that achieving Expert AGI (Level 3 AGI) marks a critical milestone denoting AI systems that reach 'at least 90th percentile of skilled adults' in a broad range of tasks, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption. Therefore, it is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The benchmark focuses on college-level subjects which might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. Some subjects like law and linguistics were ruled out because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, though strong performance should be necessary.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: MMMU is designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It is divided into a few-shot development set (150 questions, 5 per subject), a validation set (~900 questions, useful for hyperparameter selection), and a test set (10.5K questions). MMMU is designed to measure three essential skills in LMMs: perception, knowledge, and reasoning. Used for benchmarking/testing/validation of multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence.
